title: An Integrated Steady-State Axis Framework for Computational Wellness: A Cross-Modal Mapping Between Traditional Chinese Medicine, Western Pathophysiology, and Compliance-Aware Reasoning
abstract: We describe a computational wellness framework that maps eight physiologically-grounded steady-state axes (A–H) between traditional Chinese medicine terminology, Western pathophysiological pathways, and jurisdiction-aware output filters. Unlike prior efforts that treat traditional and integrative medicine as qualitative overlays, the framework exposes each axis as a scored, threshold-parameterized unit with an explicit structural causal model over inter-axis coupling. Axes I–J are declared as reserved extensions and are not implemented in the current engine; they are excluded from all fusion outputs and validation metrics in this preprint. We provide (1) an evidence-stratified case database in which 7 entries carry Crossref-verified DOIs, 8 trace to traditional Chinese medical sources, 14 are honestly labeled unverified_no_publication, and 91 are explicitly flagged synthetic_validation fixtures, (2) a cross-modal terminology mapping table (GB/T 20348 <-> axes <-> pathways <-> classical texts), (3) an eight-axis structural causal simulator producing counterfactual trajectories, prior-uncertainty bands, and E-value sensitivity analysis, and (4) a compliance layer enforcing jurisdiction-specific output restrictions across five legal regimes (CN, US, UK, EU, AU) via a fail-closed claims engine. All 1781 automated tests pass. The framework is not a diagnostic or therapeutic system; it is a well-defined computational reference for integrative wellness signaling, designed for independent replication and longitudinal data integration.
funding: This work was conducted as independent open-source research with no external funding. All software is distributed under the project's open-source license.
competing_interests: The authors declare no competing interests. HealthLens operates as an open-source wellness platform and does not sell the framework described in this preprint.
data_availability: The case evidence database, terminology mapping, calibration baselines, and DOI verification results are available at the Zenodo DOI cited in the Data Availability Statement (see data_availability_statement.md).
ethics: This study did not involve human subjects and did not require institutional review board approval. All quantitative analysis is based on publicly documented evidence and synthetic fixtures explicitly labeled as such.
confidentiality: No private health information is included in the submitted materials. The case evidence database has been audited via tools/redact_for_public_release.py with three independent fail-loud defenses against upstream bibliographic leakage.
reproducibility: All reported numerical results can be reproduced by running `python tools/engine_validation.py` (validation battery: reproducibility / specificity / coverage / domain-expectation concordance) and `python tools/reliability_bootstrap.py` (input-perturbation bootstrap: per-axis ICC and weighted Kappa, seed 20261017) against the current codebase. The validation snapshot mechanism uses git-SHA + timestamp naming to prevent silent overwrite.
limitations: The framework is a wellness reference, not a diagnostic or therapeutic system.

The case library (n=120) is stratified honestly: 7 entries carry Crossref-verified DOIs, 8 trace to traditional Chinese medical sources, 14 are labeled unverified_no_publication, and 91 are synthetic_validation fixtures. Only 15/120 (12.5%) entries have an independently verifiable source; this coverage is stated, not rounded.

The structural causal simulator's coupling coefficients are heuristic prior beliefs, not causally identified parameters; sensitivity is quantified via E-value analysis but not formally tested against prospective cohort data. The reported "prior-uncertainty bands" propagate the ±20% coupling and 0.85–1.0 adherence priors through bootstrap and are NOT empirical calibration against observed outcomes.
No longitudinal human data has been collected as of the submission date; the n-of-1 tracking data infrastructure is provided but empty.
The compliance layer is tested across five legal regimes but has not been legally reviewed by qualified practitioners in any jurisdiction.
